thread.document:
For this Special Participation E, I built an interactive DDPM (diffusion) tutor using a custom prompt in ChatGPT’s Study Mode.

The tutor walks through the standard DDPM pipeline in four modules: (1) the forward noising process and the closed-form q(x_t | x_0), (2) the reverse process p_θ(x_{t-1} | x_t) and noise prediction ε_θ(x_t, t), (3) the simplified “MSE on noise” training objective that comes from the ELBO / Gaussian KLs, (4) the sampling loop (from x_T ~ N(0, I) back to x_0), plus simple variants like DDIM and classifier-free guidance.

In each module, the tutor:

explains the intuition and minimal formulas,

asks me concept-check questions,

and gives a slightly flawed statement for me to critique (e.g., “q(x_t | x_0) always has mean zero,” “perfect ε-prediction still produces blurry samples,” or “training only at t=1 is enough”).

This makes the interaction feel more like a guided oral exam than just reading the DDPM paper again. It helped me straighten out the roles of q(x_t | x_0), p_θ, the noise schedule, and the training loss, and forced me to actively explain and defend my answers instead of passively skimming notes.

Full conversation (with the custom tutor prompt and my answers) is here: https://chatgpt.com/share/69368380-c428-800e-9481-c415a96d1deb
